# Assumptions ledger

*Generated by `python -m sfp.cli assumptions` on 2026-08-23. Do not edit by hand --
edit the YAML in `sfp/models/params/` and regenerate.*

The challenge brief asks entrants to distinguish supplied data, measured data,
assumptions and invented values. Every numerical parameter in this project
carries a provenance tag in its definition, and this file is rendered from those
tags. If a number is used by a model, it appears below.

## Provenance levels

- **`supplied`** -- Given by the challenge brief, or a design input chosen by the user at run time.
- **`measured`** -- Taken from a real dataset. Traceable to a named source.
- **`literature`** -- Taken from a cited publication. The citation is recorded with the value.
- **`assumed`** -- Engineering judgement. Defensible and order-of-magnitude right, but not sourced.
- **`invented`** -- Placeholder with no external basis. Treat any result that is sensitive to these with suspicion.

## What this ledger does not cover

Three classes of assumption are structural rather than numerical, and so cannot
be tagged on a parameter. They are recorded here explicitly:

1. **Model form.** Each subsystem is a lumped, control-oriented reduced-order
   model, not a distributed one. The choice of *which* physics to keep is itself
   an assumption; the rationale is documented in each module's docstring, with
   the source paper named.

2. **Calcium looping at ambient CO2 partial pressure.** The dynamic Ca-looping
   model this project draws on (Cormos & Simon, 2013) is a post-combustion
   model, where CO2 is a percent-level fraction of the gas. Direct air capture
   works at 420 ppm, where carbonation kinetics are far slower -- which is why
   real systems such as Carbon Engineering's put a KOH contactor and causticiser
   upstream of the CaCO3/CaO loop rather than contacting CaO with air directly.
   The brief specifies calcium looping, so it is modelled as specified, with the
   rate constants reparameterised for ambient partial pressure. Any absolute
   capture rate from this model should be read as indicative.

3. **Weather provenance is per-run, not global.** PVGIS TMY data is `measured`;
   the offline synthetic fallback is `invented`. Every run records which it used
   and the report prints it. A result generated on synthetic weather is not a
   result about a real site.


## Parameters by subsystem

### `aggregate`

PLACEHOLDER for milestone M0 only. A single lumped power-to-methane block standing in for the whole chain (air contactor -> calciner -> electrolyser -> Sabatier). It exists so the end-to-end pipeline -- weather, dispatch, report, baseline comparison -- can be closed and tested before the real reduced-order models land in M1. It is replaced, not extended.
Its one honest feature is that it has a warm-up state and a minimum load, so start/stop decisions already cost something and the scheduling problem is not trivially greedy. Everything else about it is an aggregate stand-in and every number below is tagged accordingly.

| Parameter | Value | Units | Provenance | Source / note |
| --- | ---: | --- | --- | --- |
| `rated_power_kw` | 350 | kW | `supplied` | Design input: total electrical rating of the process chain. |
| `cooldown_time_s` | 14400 | s | `assumed` | Time constant for stored heat to bleed away when idle. |
| `max_ramp_kw_per_s` | 2 | kW/s | `assumed` | Aggregate ramp limit; the real chain's is set by the Sabatier thermal response. |
| `min_load_fraction` | 0.15 | - | `assumed` | Below this the chain cannot run at all (set by the electrolyser's gas crossover limit in the real model). Forces genuine on/off commitment. |
| `part_load_penalty` | 0.18 | - | `assumed` | Specific energy consumption rises at part load by this fraction at minimum load, falling linearly to zero at rated. Stands in for the electrolyser polarisation curve; the real model derives it from cell voltage. |
| `specific_energy_kwh_per_kg` | 30 | kWh/kg_CH4 | `assumed` | Aggregate electricity per kg of methane. Built up as ~25 kWh/kg for electrolysis + methanation at ~55 % LHV efficiency (CH4 LHV 13.9 kWh/kg), plus ~5 kWh/kg for direct air capture at ~2 MWh/tCO2 and 2.75 kg CO2 per kg CH4. Superseded by the real chain in M1. *(perturbed in the truth simulator, sigma=10%)* |
| `standby_power_kw` | 8 | kW | `assumed` | Parasitic load when warm but not producing (controls, instruments, purge). |
| `startup_energy_kwh` | 120 | kWh | `assumed` | Energy to bring the chain from cold to operating temperature. |
| `warmup_time_s` | 2700 | s | `assumed` | Time constant to reach full production from cold. Represents the kiln's thermal inertia, which dominates the real chain's start-up cost. |

### `battery`

Lithium-iron-phosphate battery with a bidirectional inverter, modelled as an energy reservoir with split charge/discharge efficiency and a differentiable capacity-fade state. LFP is the right chemistry for a remote solar plant: cycle life and thermal safety matter far more than energy density.

| Parameter | Value | Units | Provenance | Source / note |
| --- | ---: | --- | --- | --- |
| `capacity_kwh` | 1000 | kWh | `supplied` | Nameplate usable energy. A design input from the CLI / siting sweep. |
| `power_kw` | 400 | kW | `supplied` | Continuous charge and discharge power limit (0.4C at the default size). |
| `calendar_fade_per_year` | 0.015 | 1/yr | `literature` | Typical LFP calendar ageing at moderate temperature and mid SoC |
| `cycle_life` | 6000 | cycles | `literature` | Manufacturer LFP datasheets, 80 % capacity retention at 80 % DoD *(perturbed in the truth simulator, sigma=20%)* |
| `end_of_life_fade` | 0.2 | - | `literature` | Industry convention: end of life at 20 % capacity fade |
| `eta_charge` | 0.96 | - | `literature` | Typical LFP one-way DC efficiency; round trip ~0.92 with the inverter *(perturbed in the truth simulator, sigma=2%)* |
| `eta_discharge` | 0.96 | - | `literature` | Typical LFP one-way DC efficiency *(perturbed in the truth simulator, sigma=2%)* |
| `self_discharge_per_day` | 0.002 | 1/d | `literature` | Typical LFP self-discharge, ~2-3 %/month at 25 degC |
| `capex_per_kwh` | 250 | EUR/kWh | `assumed` | Installed cost of storage, 2024 utility-scale. Feeds both the LCOM objective and the degradation charge the controller pays per cycle. *(perturbed in the truth simulator, sigma=20%)* |
| `soc_initial` | 0.5 | - | `assumed` | Cold-start state of charge. |
| `soc_max` | 0.95 | - | `assumed` | Upper limit; LFP calendar life suffers at a sustained 100 % SoC. |
| `soc_min` | 0.1 | - | `assumed` | Lower operating limit. Reserved headroom below this is what lets the plant ride through a fault without a black start, so the controller treats it as a hard constraint and never plans into it. |

### `economics`

The economic performance index. The README's third observation was that "efficiently" is not a well-posed objective for this plant, and it is right: maximising methane, maximising energy efficiency and maximising utilisation are three different policies. This file pins down one number instead -- the levelised cost of methane, EUR per kg CH4 -- and every controller is judged on it. It doubles as the siting tool's headline output.
Costs are 2024 European utility-scale estimates. They are assumptions, not quotes, and the LCOM is therefore a comparative instrument: use it to rank strategies and sites, not as a bankable cost.

| Parameter | Value | Units | Provenance | Source / note |
| --- | ---: | --- | --- | --- |
| `co2_credit_per_kg` | 0 | EUR/kg | `assumed` | Value of the CO2 removed from air, set to zero in the base case. A carbon price is a sensitivity in the siting study, not a base-case assumption. |
| `curtailment_penalty_per_kwh` | 0 | EUR/kWh | `assumed` | Deliberately zero. Off-grid there is no counterfactual buyer for curtailed solar, so curtailment has no direct cost -- it is a *symptom*, reported because the brief asks for it, not a term to be optimised away. Charging for it would bias the controller into cycling the battery pointlessly. |
| `discount_rate` | 0.07 | 1/yr | `assumed` | Real WACC for a merchant renewable-fuels project. |
| `fixed_opex_fraction` | 0.03 | 1/yr | `assumed` | Annual fixed O&M as a fraction of total capex. Higher than a PV plant alone because of the chemistry. |
| `methane_price_per_kg` | 1.8 | EUR/kg | `assumed` | Value of the product. Roughly EUR 130/MWh on an LHV basis -- a green-gas price with certificates, not a wholesale natural-gas price. Used as the revenue term in the controller's objective. *(perturbed in the truth simulator, sigma=25%)* |
| `process_capex_per_kw` | 2200 | EUR/kW | `assumed` | Installed cost of the whole power-to-methane chain per kW of electrical rating: electrolyser stack and BoP, air contactor, calciner, Sabatier reactor. Dominated by the electrolyser at present-day prices. *(perturbed in the truth simulator, sigma=30%)* |
| `project_lifetime_years` | 25 | yr | `assumed` | Matches typical PV warranty life; the battery is replaced within it. |
| `pv_capex_per_kwp` | 700 | EUR/kW_p | `assumed` | Installed utility-scale PV including mounting, inverter and civils. *(perturbed in the truth simulator, sigma=20%)* |
| `startup_cost_EUR` | 40 | EUR | `assumed` | Wear-and-tear charge per process start, over and above the start-up energy. Represents thermal-cycling damage to the kiln refractory and the Sabatier catalyst. This is what stops the controller chasing every cloud. |
| `water_cost_per_m3` | 2.5 | EUR/m^3 | `assumed` | Delivered demineralised water at a remote semi-arid site. Matters more than it looks: the plant needs about 2.25 kg of water per kg of methane after condensate recycle. |

### `pv`

Fixed-tilt crystalline-silicon PV array with a central inverter. Thermal model is Faiman (IEC 61853-2), which is the model PVGIS itself uses, so the array model and the irradiance data come from the same family of assumptions.

| Parameter | Value | Units | Provenance | Source / note |
| --- | ---: | --- | --- | --- |
| `age_years` | 0 | yr | `supplied` | Plant age at the start of the simulation; a siting/economics input. |
| `capacity_kwp` | 500 | kW_p | `supplied` | Array size is a design input from the CLI / siting sweep. 500 kWp is the default reference plant used throughout the report. |
| `tilt_deg` | -1 | deg | `supplied` | Array tilt. A negative value means "choose automatically from latitude" via clearsky.optimal_fixed_tilt. |
| `albedo` | 0.2 | - | `literature` | Liu & Jordan (1960); standard green-ground albedo |
| `degradation_per_year` | 0.005 | 1/yr | `literature` | Jordan & Kurtz (2013), median c-Si degradation rate 0.5 %/yr |
| `eta_inverter` | 0.975 | - | `literature` | Typical European weighted efficiency of a utility-scale central inverter *(perturbed in the truth simulator, sigma=1%)* |
| `faiman_u0` | 25 | W/(m^2 K) | `literature` | Faiman (2008); PVGIS default for free-standing modules. Constant heat-loss coefficient. Roof-mounted arrays run hotter (u0 ~ 20). *(perturbed in the truth simulator, sigma=10%)* |
| `faiman_u1` | 6.84 | W s/(m^3 K) | `literature` | Faiman (2008); PVGIS default for free-standing modules. Wind-dependent heat-loss coefficient. *(perturbed in the truth simulator, sigma=15%)* |
| `gamma_power` | -0.0035 | 1/K | `literature` | Fraunhofer ISE, Photovoltaics Report 2024 -- mono-Si temperature coefficient of Pmax. Typical mono-Si Pmax coefficient, -0.30 to -0.40 %/K. *(perturbed in the truth simulator, sigma=8%)* |
| `irradiance_ref` | 1000 | W/m^2 | `literature` | IEC 61215 standard test conditions |
| `temp_ref_C` | 25 | degC | `literature` | IEC 61215 standard test conditions |
| `dc_ac_ratio` | 1.25 | - | `assumed` | Inverter is deliberately undersized relative to the array. Standard practice and important here: it means clipping happens at the inverter as well as at the loads, and the planner must know about both. |
| `soiling_loss` | 0.03 | - | `assumed` | Annual-average soiling for a semi-arid site with periodic cleaning. The PV-soiling *fault* in the fault library drives this well above nominal. *(perturbed in the truth simulator, sigma=30%)* |
| `surface_azimuth_deg` | 180 | deg | `assumed` | Due south (clockwise from true north). Optimal for northern-hemisphere Europe. |
| `wiring_loss` | 0.02 | - | `assumed` | DC cabling and mismatch losses. |
